Hey guys I'm a resident Olympic weightlifter at the NMU-OTS and am designing a training template for people who can't find coaching they like, or can't afford programming.

Why? In highschool I didn't have a coach, leader, or a way of keeping track of what I'd done in training so I rarely accomplished a solid set of tasks in one day. Sometimes all I did was clean and jerk, other days I neglected my training of classic lifts. The idea is to provide a simple, directed method that will keep you honest and make you your own coach. As time progresses you can change the template to fit yourself better.

How does it work? Basically I design this template with things I believe your training should touch daily. Then, you decide what exercises you will do to touch on those things and you will always log the sets, reps, and weights you complete those exercises with. This will give you something to look back at and something to build off of.

Interested? send me a direct message and tell me a little about yourself, and I will do my best to respond. From there if you're someone I'd think this program is for I'll shoot you my email. From there you email me (so I have yours) then I'll email you a Word document with the template.

NOTE: I did not invent this idea. Cal Strength used to do this and I know for a fact Donny Shankle uses this approach to training!!

I was kind of thinking the same thing. I mean, if you only want the small bottle of oil it isn't bad. But, if you get oil, wax and/or balm you can easily get into $30 a month.

To be honest, I never knew about this before about a month ago. I've had a beard since I was about 17 (minus a couple "close trims" - attachment #2 on electric trimmers), and just grew to love a couple of products. The Dollar Beard Club looks like it has the basics of what you need for beard grooming, I've just never tried the product. Maybe I will!

It has what you need to start managing the wooly monster we've grown to love. The brush and comb alone are just about enough to get my money.

But, the stache wax and beard balm would be nice to have. Especially since my beard and stache like to stay separate. So the stache has to get his own love and style, typically slightly curled. But, like I said we don't have any stores that carry beard care stuff here. The closest is 2 hours away or so. And, it's really not worth the money. Especially since most of my beard life its been all natural growth with a good brushing once in awhile. I like to let my beard be itself most of the time.

I have one of those mustaches that when I put wax in it and move it to the sides to keep it out of my mouth, it curls up on the ends like the monopoly guy. Will it always be like this or will it one day become one with my beard?
I have no answers for you. My 'stache and beard avoid each other at all costs.
